parakeet: You have to lower your standards of truth to find God, you aren't discovering reality. You're protecting an illusion. If a creator exists, it should be the most undeniable, self-evident anchor of human knowledge. It shouldn't require a lifetime of intellectual acrobatics, a library of apologetics, and a stack of unverified doctrines just to make it indistinguishable from non-existence. For centuries, skeptics have been handed the burden of proof. We've been asked, how do you explain the universe without God? But that question is a distraction. The real question, the one Christianity simply cannot escape, is why the answer to everything is completely missing from anything we can actually verify. If we cannot detect it, measure it, predict it, or distinguish it from imagination, then the word existence has lost its meaning. We don't have to prove that a hidden God doesn't exist. Theology has already done that for us by defining him into total obscurity. All we have to do is refuse to grant the exemption. The next time someone tells you that God is simply beyond human investigation, remind them of the trade-off they're making. Because a God who gets a pass from explanation isn't an answer to the mystery of life. It's just a place where they stop asking questions. There's a profound irony here. Religion tells us that the universe is a loud, deliberate proclamation of its maker. But when you look closely at reality, you find a world that is perfectly capable of explaining itself through physics, chemistry, and biology. The only place the system breaks down is when we try to find an author. If a system requires you to abandon the very tools that keep you safe and informed in the real world just to let its main character inside the room, it isn't an explanation. It's an escape. If a God exists outside of every reliable way we have to know things, then he doesn't just remain unconfirmed, he remains completely irrelevant to human knowledge.
